item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded: Welcome to WordPress. This is your first post. Edit or delete it, then start writing!

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Hi, this is a comment. To get started with moderating, editing, and deleting comments, please visit the Comments screen in the dashboard. Commenter avatars come from Gravatar.

item.title: Sample Page
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
This is an example page. It's different from a blog post because it will stay in one place and will show up in your site navigation (in most themes). Most people start with an About page that introduces them to potential site visitors. It might say something like this:

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

As a new WordPress user, you should go to your dashboard to delete this page and create new pages for your content. Have fun!

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://larchwick.local.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.title: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe: Bright and Floral
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
Ethiopia is where coffee comes from, and Yirgacheffe is one of its most famous growing areas. It sits in the south of the country, in the Gedeo zone, at roughly 1,700–2,200 meters above sea level.

Why it tastes the way it does

  • Altitude: cool nights slow the cherries down, which builds sugars and acidity.
  • Heirloom varieties: thousands of local coffee types grow side by side, which gives the cup its complex, layered flavors.
  • Washed processing: most Yirgacheffe lots are washed, which gives a very clean and bright cup.

In the cup: jasmine, lemon zest and black tea, with a light, silky body.

How we brew it

We like Yirgacheffe as a pour-over at 1:16, with water just off the boil. A light roast lets the floral notes come through. Milk tends to hide them, so try it black first.

Want to read more about the region? Wikipedia has a good overview of Yirgacheffe.

item.title: Cold Brew in 4 Simple Steps
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
Cold brew is coffee steeped in cold water for many hours instead of brewed hot. The result is smooth, sweet and low in acidity. It's perfect for summer, and it keeps in the fridge for up to a week.

The recipe

  1. Grind 100 g of coffee extra coarse, like cracked pepper.
  2. Mix it with 800 g of cold, filtered water in a large jar. Stir so all the grounds are wet.
  3. Steep for 12–18 hours, in the fridge or at room temperature.
  4. Filter through a paper filter or a fine cloth, then store the concentrate in the fridge.

How to serve it

This recipe makes a concentrate. Mix it 1:1 with water or milk and pour it over ice. Taste it and adjust: some people like it stronger, others lighter.

Tip: chocolatey, nutty coffees, like our Colombia Huila, make especially good cold brew.

item.title: Choosing the Right Grind Size
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
If you change one thing about your coffee routine, change your grind. Grind size controls how fast water pulls flavor out of the coffee. Finer grounds extract faster, and coarser grounds extract slower.

Grind size by brew method

How to tell if you're off

  • Too fine: the coffee tastes bitter or harsh, and the brew drains slowly.
  • Too coarse: the coffee tastes sour or watery, and the brew drains too fast.

Why the grinder matters

A burr grinder makes particles of a similar size, so everything extracts at the same rate. A blade grinder makes dust and chunks at the same time, which leads to bitter and sour flavors in one cup. If you buy one piece of gear this year, make it a burr grinder.

item.title: How to Brew Pour-Over at Home
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
Pour-over is the easiest way to taste what makes a coffee special. It needs very little gear, and once you learn the rhythm it takes about four minutes.

What you need

  • A dripper and a paper filter
  • 15 g of freshly ground coffee (medium-fine)
  • 250 g of water at 92–96 °C
  • A kitchen scale and a timer

The method

  1. Rinse the paper filter with hot water and throw that water away. This removes the paper taste and warms the dripper.
  2. Add the coffee and shake the dripper gently so the bed is flat.
  3. Start the timer and pour about 30 g of water, just enough to wet all the grounds. Wait 30–45 seconds. This is the "bloom": the coffee releases gas and gets ready to extract evenly.
  4. Pour the rest slowly in small circles, keeping the water level steady. Aim to finish pouring by 2:00.
  5. Let it drain. The whole brew should take about 3:00–3:30.

Taste and adjust

If the cup tastes sour or thin, grind a little finer. If it tastes bitter or dry, grind a little coarser. Change only one thing at a time.

Good pour-over isn't about perfect technique. It's about repeating the same steps and changing one thing at a time.

Not sure which grind setting to start with? Read our guide to choosing the right grind size.

item.title: French Press: 5 Common Mistakes
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
The French press is forgiving, but it's easy to get a muddy or bitter cup. Here are the five mistakes we see most often.

1. The grind is too fine

Fine coffee passes through the metal mesh and over-extracts. That gives you sludge and bitterness. Use a coarse grind, about the size of sea salt.

2. The ratio is off

Too little coffee makes a weak, watery cup. Start with 1:15: 30 g of coffee for 450 g of water. Adjust from there.

3. The water is boiling

Boiling water pulls out harsh flavors. Let the kettle rest for about 30 seconds after it boils.

4. Skipping the stir

Dry clumps float on top and never brew. After about 4 minutes, stir the crust gently, scoop off the foam, then press slowly.

5. Leaving coffee in the press

The coffee keeps brewing as long as it touches the grounds. Pour it all out right after pressing, into cups or a separate jug.

Fix these five and your French press will taste cleaner the very next morning. To dial in further, see how to choose the right grind size.

item.title: Colombia Huila: Our House Espresso Bean
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
Every espresso we pull starts with a coffee from Huila, a mountain region in southern Colombia. Farms there sit at about 1,200–2,000 meters, between two ranges of the Andes.

Why we chose it

Huila coffees are sweet and balanced, which is what we want in an espresso. On its own it tastes of caramel, red apple and cocoa. With milk, the chocolate side gets stronger, so it works well in a flat white or cappuccino.

Colombia also has two harvests a year in many areas: a main crop and a smaller one called the mitaca. That helps us keep fresh coffee on the shelf all year.

Our roast

We roast it medium, just long enough to bring out the sweetness without any smoky or burnt taste.

The farms we buy from wash their coffee. Curious what that means? Read washed vs natural process, explained.

item.title: Washed vs Natural Process, Explained
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
A coffee bean is the seed inside a red fruit called a cherry. "Processing" is how farmers remove the fruit and dry the seed, and it changes the flavor a lot.

The two main methods

Washed

The fruit is removed right after picking. The beans are fermented in water for a short time, washed clean and then dried.

  • Taste: clean, bright, clear acidity
  • Good for: tasting the origin and variety

Natural

The whole cherry is dried in the sun with the bean still inside, for several weeks. Then the dried fruit is removed.

  • Taste: fruity, sweet, heavier body. Sometimes it tastes like berries or wine.
  • Good for: bold, fruit-forward cups

And "honey"?

Honey process sits in between: the skin is removed, but some sticky fruit is left on the bean while it dries. It's sweet, with a rounder body.

item.title: Meet Our New Roaster
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
We're happy to welcome Mira Holt as our new head roaster. (Mira is a fictional person for this demo site.)

Mira spent eight years as a barista and trainer before she moved to roasting. She knows how coffee behaves in the cup, and that's exactly what we wanted at the roaster.

Her roasting style

Mira likes to roast "for the cup, not the color". She tastes every batch the next morning and adjusts the profile until the coffee tastes sweet at every brew method, from espresso to pour-over.

I want every bag to taste the same on day one and on day twenty. Consistency is the most underrated flavor. — Mira Holt

Her daily coffee

A pour-over of whatever we're roasting that week, then one flat white in the afternoon.

Say hi to Mira at our next open roastery day.

How to brew it

item.title: About
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
About Larchwick

Small batches. Fresh roasts. No secrets.

Our story

Larchwick started in 2019 in a small garage with a second-hand 5 kg roaster, a few sacks of green coffee and one simple belief: coffee tastes best when it's roasted fresh and in small batches.

The first customers were friends and neighbours. Then a few local cafés asked for wholesale coffee, and the garage got too small. Today we roast in a small workshop, still in batches of 5–12 kg, twice a week.

How we work

We buy coffee through a small group of specialty importers who know the farms they work with. Every coffee we sell goes through blind tasting ("cupping") first, and only about one sample in five makes it onto our list.

We roast to order on Mondays and Thursdays. Nothing sits on a shelf for weeks. If a coffee is older than 30 days, we don't sell it as whole beans.

What we care about

Freshness

Every bag shows its roast date, and most orders leave the roastery within 48 hours of roasting.

Transparency

Origin, region, altitude, process and variety are printed on every label. If we don't know it, we say so.

No snobbery

Good coffee should be easy. Our brewing guides are short, practical and work with simple gear.

Our numbers

  • 2× roast days a week
  • 5–12 kg per batch
  • 4 coffees on the list at a time
  • 48 h from roaster to courier

The team

Tomas Varga, founder

Tomas started Larchwick after ten years in office jobs and many weekends of home roasting. He still does the cupping every Friday.

Mira Holt, head roaster

Mira spent eight years as a barista and trainer before moving to roasting. Read more in Meet our new roaster.

We'd rather sell four coffees we love than twenty we're not sure about. — Tomas Varga, founder

Visit the blog

item.title: FAQ
item.dc:creator: larchwick-team
item.content:encoded:
Frequently asked questions

Can't find your answer? Send us a message and we'll reply within two working days.

Orders and shipping

Where do you ship?

To every country in the European Union.

How long does delivery take?

We roast on Mondays and Thursdays and ship within 48 hours. Most orders arrive in 3–6 working days.

How much is shipping?

Shipping is a flat €5 in the EU, and free on orders over €40 (example prices for this demo).

Can I change or cancel my order?

Yes, until it's roasted. Email us as soon as possible and we'll help.

Our coffee

How fresh is your coffee?

Every bag shows its roast date. Coffee tastes best from about 5 to 30 days after roasting.

Do you sell ground coffee?

Yes. Choose whole beans or a grind for espresso, filter or French press. Whole beans stay fresh longer.

How should I store coffee?

In the original bag (it has a one-way valve) or an airtight container, away from light, heat and moisture. Don't keep it in the fridge.

Is your coffee organic?

Some of our coffees are grown without chemicals, but not all farms can afford organic certification, so we don't label it.

Subscriptions

How does the subscription work?

Choose a coffee, a size and a frequency (every 2 or 4 weeks). You save 10% on every delivery.

Can I pause or cancel?

Yes, any time. There's no minimum period.

Wholesale and classes

Do you offer wholesale?

Yes, for cafés, restaurants and offices. See our services or contact us for free samples.

Where do classes take place?

At our roastery, in groups of up to six people. All equipment is provided.

Can I visit the roastery?

We hold open roastery days a few times a year and announce them on our blog.
